jobs.title: Director, Marketing Operations
jobs.description: ABOUT PLACER.AI: Placer.ai is transforming how organizations understand the physical world. Our location analytics platform provides unprecedented visibility into locations, markets, and consumer behavior. Placer empowers thousands of customers—from Fortune 500 companies, to local governments and nonprofits— to make smarter, data-driven decisions. What sets us apart? We've built the most advanced location intelligence platform in the market while maintaining an uncompromising commitment to privacy, proving that powerful analytics and responsible data practices can coexist. Our growth reflects the market's demand: we reached $100M in annual recurring revenue within just 6 years of launching, achieved unicorn status with a $1B+ valuation in 2022, and continue to expand rapidly as one of North America's fastest-growing tech companies. We're creating a $100B+ market opportunity, and we're just getting started. Named one of Forbes America's Best Startup Employers and a Deloitte Technology Fast 500 company, we're building a culture where innovation thrives, collaboration is the norm, and every team member contributes to reshaping how the world understands location. SUMMARY: The Director of Marketing Operations will own how marketing runs at Placer.ai: the systems, the data, the lead lifecycle, and the reporting that marketing and revenue leadership use to make decisions. This role reports to the VP of Revenue Operations and works in direct support of marketing leadership. This person sets the direction and owns the architecture. The Marketing Operations Manager reporting to this role owns the day-to-day build work in HubSpot, Salesforce, and Chili Piper, so this is not the person configuring every workflow. It is the person who decides what gets built, reviews the work, unblocks the team, and makes the call on what we buy, keep, or retire. Marketing Operations at Placer.ai sits inside Revenue Operations, and partners with Sales Operations, Customer Success Operations, Deal Desk, and Business Operations. The funnel is managed as one system, which means this role is accountable for definitions and data that marketing and sales both rely on, not only for marketing's own reporting. This person will be the operational voice in marketing planning conversations, and will need to say clearly when a plan will not work as designed, early enough for it to matter. RESPONSIBILITIES: Own the marketing operations roadmap: what gets fixed, what gets built, and in what order, sequenced against marketing and revenue goals rather than against inbound request volume. Own marketing systems architecture and the integrity of data moving between HubSpot and Salesforce. This includes the object and field model, sync behavior, enrichment, deduplication, and account and contact matching. Where marketing and sales reporting disagree, this role is accountable for finding out why and resolving it with Sales Operations. Own the lead lifecycle end to end: stage definitions, qualification criteria, scoring thresholds, routing logic, service levels, and the handoff into sales. Get marketing and sales to agree on those definitions and then hold the line on them, including when a quarter is going badly and the definitions come under pressure. Own campaign operations and attribution. Build the measurement so that campaign performance can be defended in an executive review, and be explicit about what the model can and cannot claim about influence. Own funnel and conversion reporting as the single source of truth for marketing performance. Deliver a recommendation with the numbers rather than a dashboard and a shrug. Own marketing technology strategy, including build-versus-buy decisions, vendor evaluations, renewals, consolidation, and the cost of the stack. Bring a recommendation with the trade-offs stated, not a vendor comparison grid. Own governance for marketing systems: who can change what, how changes get tested before they ship, and how they get documented. This role writes the requirements rather than describing the problem and waiting for someone else to spec it. Own marketing data compliance in practice, including consent capture, suppression, and unsubscribe handling, working with Legal where a position needs to be set. Manage, coach, and grow the team, and hire and lead the additions to the team as it expands. Set priorities so the team is working on the highest-value problems rather than absorbing every request that arrives. Partner with Enablement and Sales Operations so that changes to routing, lifecycle, or definitions reach the field with the context they need, rather than landing as a surprise. REQUIREMENTS: Must be credible in the systems without being the primary builder. This role needs someone who can open HubSpot or Salesforce, inspect the configuration, and form an independent judgment about whether the work is right, while spending most of their time on strategy, architecture, and prioritization. Candidates who have only operated at the strategy layer, and candidates who want to spend their days building workflows, are both a poor fit. 7+ years in marketing operations, revenue operations, or a closely related function, including at least 2 years managing people. Our growth reflects the market's demand: we reached $100M in annual recurring revenue within just 6 years of launching, achieved unicorn status with a $1B+ valuation in 2022, and continue to expand rapidly as one of North America's fastest-growing tech companies. We're creating a $100B+ market opportunity, and we're just getting started. Named one of Forbes America's Best Startup Employers and a Deloitte Technology Fast 500 company, we're building a culture where innovation thrives, collaboration is the norm, and every team member contributes to reshaping how the world understands location. SUMMARY: Placer.ai is seeking a VP, Revenue Marketing to lead the strategy and execution that convert marketing investment into revenue. This person will own Strategic ABM, paid media, SEO/AEO, and the website as a single, integrated demand engine, accountable for qualified pipeline that converts through both Sales and self-serve. They will also set the standard for how the team operates, embedding AI into core workflows to inform operations at scale. This is a high-accountability role, reporting to the CMO and working in close partnership with Sales, RevOps, Product, and CS. Pipeline, product-qualified conversion and usage are shared outcomes, and this person is expected to substantiate performance with rigorous data. RESPONSIBILITIES: Forecast and own the demand plan: build and maintain a rolling pipeline forecast by channel and segment. Design and lead the Strategic team's ABM program: define account tiers, map buying committees, and orchestrate coordinated outreach across paid, direct, and sales-assisted channels in partnership with Strategic sales leadership. Direct paid media strategy: own budget and performance across SEM, paid social, and display, and make disciplined investment decisions grounded in lead quality and pipeline efficiency. Partner with content on SEO/AEO strategy, bringing conversion and revenue data to keyword, topic, and page prioritization so organic and AI-search investment is judged on pipeline contribution, not just traffic or rankings. Optimize the full funnel with precision: identify conversion drop-off at each stage, sales-assisted and self-serve alike, and lead the experimentation, page changes, and process improvements required to close the gap. Partner on product-led growth: work cross functionally to define and act on product-qualified lead signals, connecting self-serve activity to the broader pipeline plan. Own pipeline and conversion as the measure of success: set and deliver targets for qualified pipeline generated and influenced across both sales-assisted and self-serve motions, anchored to opportunity creation, product-qualified conversion, and win rate. Own efficiency metrics: track and improve CAC (blended and by channel/segment), pipeline velocity, and marketing-sourced/influenced revenue as a percentage of spend, and use those numbers to make the case for where the budget should and shouldn't go. Embed AI into the operating model: apply Claude and MCP-connected data sources to streamline reporting and campaign QA, increasing team output. REQUIREMENTS: 10+ years of progressive experience in demand generation, growth, or performance marketing, with a track record of owning the function within a B2B SaaS organization that sells through both sales-assisted and self-serve motions. Experience owning pipeline forecasting and being held to it, comfortable presenting a forecast to leadership and explaining variance. Fluency with CAC, LTV:CAC, and pipeline efficiency metrics as core operating KPIs, with a track record of using them to reallocate budget. Demonstrated success building and running a Strategic/enterprise ABM program, with fluency in account tiering, ABM technology, and multi-channel orchestration. Working fluency in PLG mechanics — product-qualified leads, self-serve conversion, usage-based triggers — and how they operate alongside a Strategic sales funnel. A proven record of managing SEM, paid social, and display at scale, with the judgment to reallocate or cut spend based on performance. Strong command of SEO fundamentals and current knowledge of AEO/answer-engine optimization, with experience owning a website's conversion performance. Sophisticated fluency in attribution and funnel analytics, with the judgment to act on data. Hands-on experience with marketing automation and CRM platforms (HubSpot, Marketo, Salesforce, or equivalent) and the reporting infrastructure built on them. Demonstrated people leadership, having built and developed a high-performing demand generation or growth team.&
